literal: Mu Chong
idiomatic: Biography of Mu Chong

literal: His forebears for generations showed loyal service in the ages of Emperor Shenyuan and the Huan and Mu emperors.
idiomatic: His line had served with loyalty since the reigns of Emperor Shenyuan and the Huan and Mu emperors.

literal: Chong was nimble and quick-witted; in youth he made theft his occupation.
idiomatic: Chong was sharp and agile; in his youth he lived by theft.

literal: When Taizu dwelt in the Dugu tribe, Chong constantly came and went supplying him—no one of the time could match it.
idiomatic: While Taizu stayed with the Dugu tribe, Chong went back and forth to provision him as no one else could.

literal: Later, when Liu Xian plotted rebellion, Emperor Pingwen's maternal grandson Liang Juan learned of it and secretly sent Chong to inform Taizu.
idiomatic: Later, when Liu Xian plotted treason, Liang Juan—Emperor Pingwen's grandson by a daughter—learned of the plot and secretly sent Chong to warn Taizu.

literal: Juan said to Chong: "If Xian learns of it and questions you, a man should die for principle; though swords cut and carve you apart, do not reveal it.
idiomatic: Juan told Chong, "If Xian finds out and questions you, a man must die for his lord; let them cut you with swords—do not speak.

literal: " He therefore gave Chong his favored wife and the fine horse he rode, saying, "If the matter is exposed, I shall use these to clear myself.
idiomatic: He gave Chong his favorite wife and his best horse, saying, "If we are found out, I will clear myself with these."

literal: " Chong came to report the peril; Taizu galloped to the Helan tribe.
idiomatic: Chong brought word of danger; Taizu galloped to the Helan tribe.

literal: Xian indeed suspected Juan had leaked the plot and was about to imprison him.
idiomatic: Xian indeed suspected Juan had betrayed the plot and was about to seize him.

literal: Chong then proclaimed aloud: "Liang Juan has forgotten grace and righteousness and would back Xian in rebellion; today I have seized his wife and horse—enough to settle the score.
idiomatic: Chong then shouted aloud, "Liang Juan has forgotten grace and would make Xian rebel! I have taken his wife and horse—that settles the score."

literal: " Xian heard and believed it.
idiomatic: Xian heard him and believed it.

literal: In Kudou's turmoil, Chong's sister's son Yu Huan and others plotted to seize Taizu in collusion;[1] they told Chong: "Kudou is already established, the masses all submit—wealth and rank must not be missed; I beg you, uncle, to plan for it.
idiomatic: During Kudou's revolt, Chong's nephew Yu Huan and others plotted to seize Taizu in collusion;[1] they told Chong, "Kudou already holds the throne and all men rally to him—fortune like this is not to be lost. Uncle, we beg you to join us."

literal: " Chong then by night informed Taizu; Taizu executed Huan and the rest, crossed north over the Yin Mountains, and again came in fortune to the Helan tribe.
idiomatic: Chong warned Taizu by night; Taizu executed Huan and his fellows, crossed the Yin Mountains to the north, and again took refuge with the Helan tribe.

literal: Chong was greatly favored and treated with honor.
idiomatic: Chong stood in the highest favor.

literal: When Taizu became Prince of Wei, Chong was appointed General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.
idiomatic: When Taizu was made Prince of Wei, Chong received the rank of General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.

literal: He followed in pacifying the Central Plains and was granted the title Duke of Liyang and made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: He marched in the pacification of the Central Plains and was enfeoffed Duke of Liyang with the post of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: Later he was moved to Grand Commandant, added Palace Attendant, and transferred to Duke of Anyi.
idiomatic: He was later promoted to Grand Commandant, given the added title of palace attendant, and advanced to Duke of Anyi.

literal: He again followed the campaign against the Gaoche and returned with a great victory.
idiomatic: He joined the campaign against the Gaoche and came back in triumph.

literal: Yao Xing besieged Luoyang; Sima Dezong's general Xin Gongjing requested rescue, and Taizu sent Chong with six thousand horse to go to his aid.
idiomatic: When Yao Xing besieged Luoyang, Xin Gongjing, general under Sima Dezong, begged for relief; Taizu sent Chong with six thousand riders.

literal: Before he arrived, Gongjing was defeated; an edict ordered Chong to garrison Ye at once, made him Inspector of Yuzhou, and he retained his former general's rank.
idiomatic: Chong had not yet arrived when Gongjing fell; an edict set him to garrison Ye immediately, named him inspector of Yuzhou, and left him his former general's rank.

literal: He was summoned as Grand Commandant and again transferred to Duke of Yidu.
idiomatic: He was recalled to Grand Commandant and again advanced to Duke of Yidu.

literal: In the third year of Tianci he died.
idiomatic: He died in the third year of Tianci.

literal: Earlier, when Prince Wei Yi plotted rebellion, Chong took part beforehand; Taizu, cherishing his merit, kept it secret.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Prince Wei Yi plotted treason, Chong had been party to it; Taizu, valuing his service, concealed the matter.

literal: When the responsible offices memorialized on the posthumous name, Taizu personally reviewed the posthumous statutes; at "Unable to Fulfill Righteous Intent" the syllable was "Ding."
idiomatic: When the offices submitted a posthumous name, Taizu read the statutes himself; at the entry "Unable to Fulfill Righteous Intent" he came to the syllable Ding.

literal: Taizu said: "This fits.
idiomatic: Taizu said, "That is the one."

literal: " He therefore gave the posthumous title Lord Ding.
idiomatic: He therefore posthumously named him Lord Ding.

literal: Earlier, when Taizu fled Kudou's turmoil, he sent Chong back to observe men's hearts.
idiomatic: Earlier, fleeing Kudou's revolt, Taizu had sent Chong back to gauge where loyalties lay.

literal: Chong came at night among the people, left his horse with attendants, and in plain dress entered their camp.
idiomatic: Chong reached the camps by night, left his horse with his men, and went in disguised.

literal: There happened to be firelight; a woman pounding grain recognized him, and the bandits all sprang up in alarm.
idiomatic: Firelight betrayed him; a woman at the mortar recognized him, and the rebels leapt up in alarm.

literal: Chong could not find his attendants; he hid in a pit, then slowly stole a horse and fled.
idiomatic: Unable to find his men, he hid in a pit, then slowly stole a horse and fled.

literal: He lodged in the great marsh; a white wolf came toward Chong and howled; Chong took warning, galloped after the wolf, and thus escaped peril.
idiomatic: He spent the night in a great marsh; a white wolf howled at him; taking it as a sign, he galloped after the wolf and escaped.

literal: He had just gone when the pursuers of the rebel band arrived, and so he escaped danger.
idiomatic: He had barely gone when the rebel pursuers arrived; thus he slipped free.

literal: Taizu marveled at it and ordered Chong to establish a shrine; descendants for generations have offered sacrifice.
idiomatic: Taizu marveled and ordered a shrine to Chong; descendants have sacrificed there ever since.

literal: In the Taihe era, when meritorious subjects were recorded, Chong was granted joint sacrifice.
idiomatic: When the Taihe court recorded founding merit, Chong was admitted to joint sacrifice at the ancestral temple.

literal: Chong's eldest son Suiliu held distinguished offices through the years.
idiomatic: Chong's eldest son Suiliu rose through a series of high posts.

literal: In campaigning against the Rouran he had merit and was granted Marquis of Lingling.
idiomatic: For merit against the Rouran he was enfeoffed Marquis of Lingling.

literal: Later he was dismissed for crime.
idiomatic: He was later stripped of rank for a crime.

literal: His son Yijiu was a man of mature conduct within the palace.
idiomatic: His son Yijiu was esteemed within the palace for upright conduct.

literal: For merit he was granted Duke of Fucheng, made General Who Establishes Loyalty, and moved to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Bearer of the Imperial Household Yellow Gate, and Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Fucheng and named General Who Establishes Loyalty, then rose to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, bearer of the imperial household yellow gate, and palace attendant.

literal: He died; posthumous name Jing.
idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Jing.

literal: His son Zhen began his career as Central Scribe, was transferred to attend the Eastern Palace, married the Princess of Changcheng, and was made Commandant of Cavalry Escort.
idiomatic: His son Zhen began as central scribe, was moved to attend the heir apparent, married the Princess of Changcheng, and became commandant of cavalry escort.

literal: Later an edict ordered divorce; he took the elder sister of Empress Dowager Wenming.
idiomatic: Later an edict forced divorce; he married Empress Dowager Wenming's elder sister.

literal: Soon he was made Southern Department Minister and Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: Before long he was named southern department minister and palace attendant.

literal: He died; posthumous name Xuan.
idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Xuan.

literal: Gaozu, recalling Chong's merit, ordered Compiler Han Xianzong and Zhen together to fix the text of a stele and erect it on Mount Bai.
idiomatic: Gaozu, remembering Chong's service, ordered Han Xianzong of the compilation bureau and Zhen to draft a stele and set it up on Mount Bai.

literal: Zhen's son Tai, original name Shiluo, was given his present name by Gaozu.
idiomatic: Zhen's son Tai, originally named Shiluo, received his new name from Gaozu.

literal: As a meritorious descendant he married the Princess of Zhangwu Chang, was made Commandant of Cavalry Escort, put in charge of the Four Bureaus of the Imperial Hunt, and granted Marquis of Fengyi.
idiomatic: As a meritorious scion he married the Princess of Zhangwu Chang, became commandant of cavalry escort, oversaw the four bureaus of the imperial hunt, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Fengyi.

literal: He was moved to Palace Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat and added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Stabilizes the West.
idiomatic: He was promoted to palace supervisor of the imperial secretariat with the added titles of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and general who stabilizes the west.

literal: His rank was advanced to duke.
idiomatic: He was raised from marquis to duke.

literal: He went out as General Who Stabilizes the South and Governor of Luo.
idiomatic: He went out as general who stabilizes the south and governor of Luo.

literal: By precedent his rank was reduced to marquis.
idiomatic: Under standing rules he stepped down one grade to marquis.

literal: Soon he was summoned as Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as right grand master for splendid happiness and right vice director of the imperial secretariat.

literal: He again went out as Bearer of Staff with Full Powers, General Who Stabilizes the North, and Governor of Ding.
idiomatic: He went out again as bearer of staff with full powers, general who stabilizes the north, and governor of Ding.

literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Fengyi, state-founding, with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: His fief was changed to state-founding Marquis of Fengyi with five hundred households.

literal: He was advanced to General Who Campaigns North.
idiomatic: He was promoted to general who campaigns north.

literal: At first Empress Dowager Wenming had confined Gaozu in a separate chamber and was about to plot deposition and removal; Tai remonstrated sharply and she stopped.
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming first confined Gaozu apart and plotted to depose him, Tai remonstrated fiercely and she desisted.

literal: Gaozu was grateful for his virtue and therefore bestowed on him mountains-and-rivers reward, favoring him to the utmost.
idiomatic: Gaozu owed him gratitude, granted him the mountains-and-rivers reward, and favored him to the summit.

literal: Tai himself reported long illness and begged for Heng Province; Lu Rui was therefore transferred to Ding Province and Tai took his place.
idiomatic: Tai pleaded chronic illness and asked for Heng Province; Lu Rui was moved to Ding and Tai replaced him.

literal: Tai did not wish to see the capital moved; before Rui could set out Tai had already arrived, and they secretly incited one another, plotting rebellion.
idiomatic: Unwilling to see the capital moved, Tai reached his post before Rui could depart; the two secretly stirred each other toward rebellion.

literal: He then with Rui and Marquis of Anle Yuan Long, Garrison Commander of Fuming and Marquis of Lu Commandery Yuan Ye, Valiant Cavalry General Yuan Chao, Marquis of Yangping He Tou, Commandant of Archers Who Shoot at Sound Yuan Yueping, former Garrison Commander of Pengcheng Yuan Ba, Administrator of Dai Commandery Yuan Zhen, General Who Stabilizes the North and Prince of Leling Siyu, and others plotted to set up Yi, Prince of Yangping and Inspector of Shuozhou, as ruler.
idiomatic: He then conspired with Rui, Yuan Long Marquis of Anle, Yuan Ye garrison commander of Fuming and Marquis of Lu, Yuan Chao valiant cavalry general, He Tou Marquis of Yangping, Yuan Yueping commandant of archers who shoot at sound, Yuan Ba former garrison commander of Pengcheng, Yuan Zhen administrator of Dai, Siyu general who stabilizes the north and Prince of Leling, and others to make Yi, Prince of Yangping in Shuozhou, their sovereign.

literal: Yi did not follow them; he falsely assented to calm them and secretly memorialized the matter.
idiomatic: Yi would not join them; he feigned assent to quiet them and reported the plot in a secret memorial.

literal: Gaozu then sent Prince Cheng of Rencheng to raise Bing and Si troops to attack them.
idiomatic: Gaozu sent Prince Cheng of Rencheng with troops from Bing and Si to suppress them.

literal: Cheng first sent Attendant-in-Ordinary who Investigates Documents Li Huan alone on horseback into Dai, taking them unawares; Tai and the rest were alarmed and had no plan.
idiomatic: Cheng first sent Li Huan, attendant-in-ordinary who investigates documents, alone on horseback into Dai to catch them off guard; Tai and his party were thrown into panic with no plan left.

literal: Huan enlightened the rebels with gain and loss, showing fortune and calamity; the wicked party lost heart and none would serve them.
idiomatic: Huan explained fortune and ruin to the rebels; the plotters lost heart and none would fight for them.

literal: Tai judged he must fail and led his followers—several hundred men—to attack Huan at the outer gate, hoping for one victory.
idiomatic: Seeing defeat inevitable, Tai led several hundred men against Huan at the outer gate, hoping for a single stroke of luck.

literal: He could not take it; alone on horseback he fled out the west gate and was seized and sent in.
idiomatic: He failed, fled alone through the west gate, was captured, and sent to the capital.

literal: Cheng also soon arrived and thoroughly prosecuted the party.
idiomatic: Cheng arrived soon after and prosecuted the conspiracy to the end.

literal: Gaozu came to Dai, personally saw the culprits, questioned them on their rebellion, and Tai and the rest were executed.
idiomatic: Gaozu came to Dai, questioned the rebels himself, and Tai and his fellows were executed.

literal: His son Bozhi, at eight sui attended study in the Eastern Palace; at ten he was made Palace Groom and Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.
idiomatic: His son Bozhi entered the Eastern Palace school at eight; at ten he was made palace groom and supernumerary cavalier attendant.

literal: He married the Princess of Raoyang and was made Commandant of Cavalry Escort.
idiomatic: He married the Princess of Raoyang and became commandant of cavalry escort.

literal: He died young.
idiomatic: He died before his time.

literal: His son Jie.
idiomatic: His son was Jie.

literal: Bozhi's younger brother Shiru, style name Shuxian.
idiomatic: Bozhi's younger brother Shiru, styled Shuxian.

literal: He was moved to Liang Province; only later was he able to return.
idiomatic: He was relocated to Liang Province and was able to return only later.

literal: He was made aide to the Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He served as aide to the Grand Commandant.

literal: His son Rong, in the Wuding era, was Administrator of Ji commandery.
idiomatic: His son Rong was administrator of Ji commandery in the Wuding era.

literal: Yijiu's younger brother Niutou was Palace Attendant and Northern Department Minister.
idiomatic: Yijiu's younger brother Niutou served as palace attendant and northern department minister.

literal: He died; posthumously made Lord of Works and given posthumous name Jing.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named lord of works with the posthumous title Jing.

literal: His son Puban was Minister of the Imperial Stud, General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, and Inspector of Jing.
idiomatic: His son Puban was minister of the imperial stud, general who campaigns against the barbarians, and inspector of Jing.

literal: Posthumously made General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of Yong; posthumous name Zhao.
idiomatic: He was posthumously named general who campaigns west and inspector of Yong, with the posthumous title Zhao.

literal: His son Shao, style name Fuxing, was Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant, Administrator of Dai Commandery, General Who Campaigns East, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple cord.
idiomatic: His son Shao, styled Fuxing, was supernumerary cavalier attendant, administrator of Dai commandery, general who campaigns east, and grand master for splendid happiness with golden seal and purple cord.

literal: He died; posthumously made Bearer of Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs of Ji, Xiang, and Yin provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Ji; posthumous name Wen.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named bearer of staff, commander of Ji, Xiang, and Yin military affairs, grand general of agile cavalry, and inspector of Ji, with the posthumous title Wen.

literal: His son Zunbo was Administrator of You province.
idiomatic: His son Zunbo was administrator of You province.

literal: Suiliu's younger brother Guan, style name Tabo, inherited Chong's title.
idiomatic: Suiliu's younger brother Guan, styled Tabo, inherited Chong's title.

literal: In youth he was famed for literary accomplishment; he was chosen to fill the inner attendants, and Taizu valued him.
idiomatic: In youth he was known for literary talent; chosen as inner attendant, he won Taizu's regard.

literal: When Taizong took the throne he was made Left General of the Guard, managed the Gate and Secretariat, and issued edicts.
idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he was named left general of the guard, oversaw the gate and secretariat, and issued edicts.

literal: When he inquired into old affairs, never was anything lost; Taizong marveled at it.
idiomatic: When he traced precedents, no detail ever slipped; Taizong marveled.

literal: He married the Princess of Yiyang and was made Commandant of Cavalry Escort, then gradually advanced to Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He married the Princess of Yiyang, became commandant of cavalry escort, and rose step by step to Grand Commandant.

literal: When Shizu supervised the state, Guan was his right-hand aide; going out he commanded the court, coming in he answered at the ruler's side—nothing great or small did not pass through his decision.
idiomatic: While Shizu supervised the realm, Guan was his right hand: abroad he directed government, at court he answered the heir—nothing large or small escaped his judgment.

literal: All day he was cheerful, without anger or joy on his face.
idiomatic: He remained cheerful all day, never showing anger or elation on his face.

literal: He toiled, was modest, and skillfully guided others, not arrogant because of wealth and rank.
idiomatic: He worked hard, stayed modest, and guided others well, never arrogant in wealth or rank.

literal: In the eighth year of Taichang he died suddenly of illness in the park, age thirty-five.
idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taichang he died suddenly of illness in the park at thirty-five.

literal: Taizong came in person to his funeral and grieved so that those beside him were moved.
idiomatic: Taizong attended his funeral in person and grieved until those around him wept.

literal: He was granted a coffin of gold with hidden relief over the whole body; funeral rites followed entirely the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shu Sun Jun.
idiomatic: He was given a coffin of gold with relief over the whole body; rites followed the precedent of Prince Shu Sun Jun of Ancheng.

literal: He was posthumously made Prince of Yidu with posthumous title Wencheng.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made Prince of Yidu with the title Wencheng.

literal: When Shizu took the throne, whenever he talked and feasted with the ministers he never failed to sigh with earnest praise, thinking that since Taichang there had been no founding minister combining civil and military like him—such was the praise he received.
idiomatic: After Shizu took the throne he never feasted with his ministers without sighing in praise, saying that since Taichang no founding minister had matched Guan's civil and military gifts—such was the esteem in which he was held.

literal: His son Shou inherited the title; in youth, through his father's position, he was chosen to attend the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: His son Shou inherited the title and, through his father's standing, was chosen in youth to attend the Eastern Palace.

literal: He married the Princess of Leling and was made Commandant of Cavalry Escort.
idiomatic: He married the Princess of Leling and became commandant of cavalry escort.

literal: Bright and keen, he had his father's manner; Shizu cherished and valued him and promoted him to Lower Grand Master.
idiomatic: Clever and sharp, he had his father's bearing; Shizu cherished him and promoted him to lower grand master.

literal: In memorials and debate he was quick and had a voice within and without the court.
idiomatic: His memorials and debate were nimble, and his reputation rang inside and outside the court.
